reason: The premise that Cr coatings fail by interdiffusion is supported by E3, which notes Cr coating peeling/cracking in high-temperature steam. However, the specific claims about Al2O3's barrier properties, its deposition as a thin interlayer, its compatibility with Cr2O3 formation, and its stability under the stated conditions are not supported by any of the cited evidence (E1 discusses a different alloy system, E2 discusses multi-component metallic barriers, and E3 only mentions general ATF cladding challenges).
premises: Cr coating on Zr-alloy fails prematurely at high temperature due to Cr–Zr interdiffusion
Al2O3 is chemically inert with very low ion mobility and can act as a diffusion barrier
A thin, continuous Al2O3 interlayer can be deposited between Zr-alloy and Cr coating
The Al2O3 barrier will not compromise the Cr coating's ability to form protective Cr2O3
The Al2O3 barrier will remain effective and adherent under normal and high-temperature steam conditions
